prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] Income statement · fiscal quarters (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "USD millions" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Fiscal 2024" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Full year" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "USD millions" · longest unbreakable word 104px · one-line width 454px
  col 2: header "Fiscal 2024 › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 42px
  col 3: header "Fiscal 2024 › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 45px · one-line width 45px
  col 4: header "Fiscal 2024 › Q3" · longest unbreakable word 45px · one-line width 45px
  col 5: header "Fiscal 2024 › Q4" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 44px
  col 6: header "Full year" · longest unbreakable word 54px · one-line width 68px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 553px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 552px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare income statement line items across fiscal 2024 quarters and against the full-year total, in USD millions.","reading":"Readers scan row labels to find a line item, then read across to compare quarters and the full year; they can also scan down a quarter to compare line items. The long cost-of-revenue label will create a taller row that can absorb its own wrapping.","groups":["Columns 2–5 are equivalent quarterly measures and benefit from similar widths.","Column 6 is another monetary measure but represents the full year; its distinct header needs more space if it is to stay on one line.","Column 1 identifies each row and needs most of the flexible text space."],"keep_intact":["Quarterly and full-year numeric values","Quarter identifiers Q1–Q4","Individual words in row labels and headers"],"may_wrap":["The long cost-of-revenue label at word boundaries","Research and development at word boundaries","Full year between its two words","USD millions between its two words"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [217, 63, 66, 66, 65, 75] · table 553×316px · row heights [39, 39, 39, 92, 66, 39] · column headers wrapped 1/7 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
